regions.summary: Northeast Wuhan across the Yangtze: Xinzhou district (66%) and the Qianchuan part of Huangpi (31%).

candidates.name: Xinzhou
candidates.meaning: "New islet": a county formed in 1951 (Xinzhou county), made a Wuhan district in 1998.
candidates.fit: 66% of the region's people, and the district's seat Zhucheng and Yangluo are inside.
candidates.recognisability: Current district, always known.
candidates.source_note: 1951年6月建立新洲县，1998年撤县设区

candidates.name: Huangpi
candidates.meaning: Old county name (Huangpi, 579 onward); the district seat Qianchuan is in this region.
candidates.fit: Holds 30% of the district's people and its seat; the rest of Huangpi is split over region 2 and others.
candidates.recognisability: Current district; CHGIS puts the Huangpi county seat (579-1911) here.
candidates.source_note: 区人民政府驻前川街道

regions.notes: Huangpi is also the main county of region 2's Panlongcheng area, so Huangpi here is workable only if region 2 does not use it.

regions.summary: Northwest edge of Wuhan on the Han River side: Hanchuan city (45%), Panlongcheng and Tianhe airport area of Huangpi, and Dongxihu's north.

candidates.name: Hanchuan
candidates.meaning: "Han river plain": named in 977 because the Han River runs across the county.
candidates.fit: 45% of the region's people and the county seat (Xiannvshan) is inside, though it holds only 27% of the county.
candidates.recognisability: County-level city of about 0.9M.
candidates.source_note: 977年，因汉水横贯县境，改名汉川县

candidates.name: Panlongcheng
candidates.meaning: "Coiled dragon city": the Shang dynasty walled city (about 1500 BC) beside the Fu River, the earliest known city in the Wuhan area.
candidates.fit: The site and its development zone (14% of the region) are inside; the name suits a region mixing Huangpi, Dongxihu and Hanchuan.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 251 hits with 湖北, top ones about this place.
candidates.source_note: 武汉市东北郊黄陂区境内的盘龙湖畔，南隔府河与汉口相望

regions.notes: Both are good; Panlongcheng avoids the region reading as only a Hanchuan region when Hanchuan covers just 27% of its county.

regions.summary: East Hankou: Jiang'an district (79%) with the old concessions, and the east side of Jianghan.

candidates.name: Hankou
candidates.meaning: "Mouth of the Han": the town at the Han River's junction with the Yangtze, one of the three towns of Wuhan.
candidates.fit: Jiang'an held the foreign concessions and the river front of Hankou; the other Hankou districts fall mostly in region 6 and region 4.
candidates.recognisability: One of the three towns, a treaty port and a former separate city.
candidates.source_note: 武昌、汉口、汉阳三块区域隔江鼎立

candidates.name: Jiang'an
candidates.meaning: "River bank": named for the Yangtze north bank at the Jiang'an railway station and quay.
candidates.fit: 79% of the region's people; the region holds 77% of the district.
candidates.recognisability: Current district.
candidates.source_note: 名称中的“江岸”便是指长江北岸

regions.notes: If Anita prefers Hankou for region 6 (Jianghan core), then this region takes Jiang'an.

regions.summary: West Hankou: Dongxihu district (52%) and Qiaokou (35%).

candidates.name: Dongxihu
candidates.meaning: "East-west lake": the district formed in 1958 from reclaimed lake land west of Hankou.
candidates.fit: 52% of the people, 72% of the district.
candidates.recognisability: Current district.
candidates.source_note: 1957年围垦，1958年10月设立武汉市东西湖区

candidates.name: Qiaokou
candidates.meaning: "Bridge mouth": from the stone bridge built in the 1600s where the Yudai canal met the Han River.
candidates.fit: 35% of the people; the region holds 47% of the district.
candidates.recognisability: Current district; Hanzheng Street market is here.
candidates.source_note: 在河与汉江相连处的河口，修建了一座石桥，因而此地被称之为“硚口”

regions.summary: Qingshan steel district (46%) and Hongshan's east lakeshore around Heping (41%), north of East Lake.

candidates.name: Qingshan
candidates.meaning: "Green hill": from the old Yangtze river town Qingshanji, named in the Song history and in Lu You's travel diary (1170).
candidates.fit: 46% of the people; the region holds 93% of Qingshan.
candidates.recognisability: Current district, home of the Wuhan steel works.
candidates.source_note: “青山”之名，始见于《宋史·地理志》

regions.notes: East Lake (Donghu) touches this region and region 9; it is given to region 9.

regions.summary: The centre of Wuhan at the Han-Yangtze junction: Jianghan (42%), Qiaokou (30%), parts of Jiang'an and Hanyang.

candidates.name: Wuhan
candidates.meaning: Wu(chang) plus Han(kou, Hanyang): the three towns joined as one city in 1927.
candidates.fit: The central region of the city, touching the Han mouth and holding pieces of Hankou and Hanyang; the old centre.
candidates.recognisability: The city itself, over 10M.
candidates.source_note: 1927年，国民政府将武昌、汉阳、汉口合并为武汉市

candidates.name: Jianghan
candidates.meaning: "Yangtze and Han": the district between the two rivers at their junction; also the name of the wider plain.
candidates.fit: 42% of the people; the region holds 74% of the district.
candidates.recognisability: Current district; Jianghan Road is the main shopping street.
candidates.source_note: 区境南临长江、汉江交汇处

regions.notes: Region 7 (Wuchang) is the other candidate for the plain city name; region 6 sits nearest the three towns' meeting point, so I gave it Wuhan.

regions.summary: Wuchang district (94%), the old walled city south of the Yangtze with Yellow Crane Tower.

candidates.name: Wuchang
candidates.meaning: "Martial prosperity": a Wu kingdom name (3rd century), later the seat of Wuchang prefecture and Hubei government; site of the 1911 uprising.
candidates.fit: 94% of the people and 81% of the district; the prefecture seat and Jiangxia commandery seat lay here.
candidates.recognisability: One of the three towns; the uprising of 1911.
candidates.source_note: 武昌府 (1364-1911) seated at 今湖北武汉市武昌

regions.summary: Hanyang district (89%), south of the Han River, plus the Zhuankou edge of Caidian.

candidates.name: Hanyang
candidates.meaning: "North of the Han" by yin-yang naming, though the Han shifted in the 1400s and the town now lies south of it.
candidates.fit: 89% of the people; Hanyang prefecture and county seat (621-1911) lay here.
candidates.recognisability: One of the three towns; famed for the Hanyang arsenal rifle and the Guqintai story.
candidates.source_note: 汉阳府 (1277-1911) seated at 今湖北省武汉市汉阳

regions.summary: East of Wuchang: Hongshan district's Guanshan, Luonan and Guanggu side (94%), including half of the East Lake scenic area.

candidates.name: East Lake
candidates.meaning: Donghu, the large lake inside Wuchang, once China's largest city lake.
candidates.fit: The scenic area street is 12% of the region and the East Lake high-tech zone lies here; the lake itself sits on the border with regions 5 and 7, so the fit is moderate.
candidates.recognisability: 1285 zh-wiki hits with 湖北 (many are East Lake institutions); the plain 东湖 title is a disambiguation page, the Wuhan lake article title was not confirmed.
candidates.source_note: 武昌的东湖曾为中国第一大城中湖，随着武汉市区面积不断扩大，汤逊湖现已取代东湖

candidates.name: Hongshan
candidates.meaning: Named for Hong Hill (Hongshan), renamed from East Hill in the 1230s when the Dahong mountain temple moved there.
candidates.fit: 94% of the people, but the hill and Hongshan street are mostly in region 11.
candidates.recognisability: Current district.
candidates.source_note: 洪山古名东山，南宋端平年间改东山为洪山

regions.notes: Hongshan is used for region 11 where the hill itself is.

regions.summary: Ezhou (Echeng and Huarong, 57%) and Huangzhou across the Yangtze (42%).

candidates.name: Ezhou
candidates.meaning: From E, the old state and the short name of Hubei; Wu built the city here in the 3rd century and called it Wuchang.
candidates.fit: Holds the city seat Echeng and Huarong, 59% of the people by prefecture.
candidates.recognisability: Prefecture-level city of 1.08M; origin of the Hubei abbreviation E.
candidates.source_note: 湖北简称鄂由此得名

candidates.name: Huangzhou
candidates.meaning: Yellow prefecture: seat of Huanggang prefecture since 583; the place of Su Dongpo's exile and Red Cliff poems.
candidates.fit: Holds 93% of Huangzhou district, 42% of the region's people; the prefecture seat was here.
candidates.recognisability: Current district of Huanggang city; Su Shi's Huangzhou.
candidates.source_note: 黄州府 (1364-1911) seated at 今湖北黄州市

regions.notes: The region straddles the Yangtze; Ezhou covers both Ezhou districts, Huangzhou the north bank. Check against the east Hubei agent for a Huanggang name.

regions.summary: Southwest Hongshan: Shizishan, Hongshan street, Zhangjiawan, with Baishazhou and Nanhu edges (88% Hongshan).

candidates.name: Hongshan
candidates.meaning: Hong Hill: named in the 1230s when the Dahong mountain temple was moved to East Hill.
candidates.fit: Hongshan street and Baotong Temple lie here; the region holds 17% of the district.
candidates.recognisability: Current district.
candidates.source_note: 改东山为洪山，改弥陀寺为崇宁万寿禅寺

regions.notes: Only 0.35M people; Hongshan name used here and not for region 9.

regions.summary: West of Wuhan on the Han and Yangtze: Caidian (72%), Hannan (10%), and Hanchuan's southeast (15%).

candidates.name: Caidian
candidates.meaning: Cai-dian, a Hanyang county market town and later the seat of the district; the source gives no origin of the name.
candidates.fit: 72% of the people, 82% of the district.
candidates.recognisability: Current district.
candidates.source_note: 区人民政府驻知音湖大道

regions.notes: The Caidian article gives no origin for the name.

regions.summary: Southeast of Wuhan's centre: Guanggu south and Miaoshan, Jiangxia (78%) and Hongshan's Guandong.

candidates.name: Tangxun
candidates.meaning: Tangxun Lake, now the largest lake inside a Chinese city (47.6 km2), replacing East Lake.
candidates.fit: The lake lies south of Wuchang in Hongshan and Jiangxia, which is this region; part of it may reach region 14.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 39 hits with 湖北.
candidates.source_note: 汤逊湖是中国最大的城中湖，面积约47.6平方千米

regions.notes: Jiangxia is held for region 14 where the old county seat Zhifang lies.

regions.summary: South of Wuhan: Jiangxia (57%), Gedian in Ezhou (13%), Jiayu county (10%), Zhifang and Jinkou.

candidates.name: Jiangxia
candidates.meaning: "Yangtze summer": Jiangxia commandery set up in 201 BC; the county seat moved to Wuchang in 589 and the name came back to this district in 1995.
candidates.fit: 57% of the people; the district seat Zhifang is here and the old Shayi county seat at Jinkou.
candidates.recognisability: Current district, and Han commandery.
candidates.source_note: 西汉高祖六年（前201年）设置江夏郡

regions.notes: Shayi (沙羡) has no own article and only 16 hits, so I left it out.

regions.summary: Daye city (86%) and Liangzihu district around Taihe (13%).

candidates.name: Daye
candidates.meaning: "Great smelting": county created 967 from a mining and smelting station, meaning 'great furnaces'.
candidates.fit: 86% of the people; the region holds 88% of the city.
candidates.recognisability: County-level city of about 0.9M; copper and iron mining centre.
candidates.source_note: 取“大兴炉冶”之意

regions.summary: Yangxin county (82%) in the southeast, with Xisaishan and Ruichang edges.

candidates.name: Yangxin
candidates.meaning: "Sunny new": county name used for Xingguo prefecture's seat; the source gives no origin of the name.
candidates.fit: 82% of the people, 99% of the county.
candidates.recognisability: County of 0.9M.
candidates.source_note: 兴国州 (1376-1911) seated at 今湖北阳新县

regions.notes: Xingguo (the old prefecture) is famous in Jiangxi, so it is not offered.
